question: What is the primary purpose of clinical supervision in nursing practice?

options.A: To protect public safety and develop professional competence
options.B: To replace formal hospital management disciplinary committees
options.C: To punish staff members who make minor documentation errors
options.D: To reduce the number of working hours required for nurses

explanation: Clinical supervision exists mainly to support staff growth while safeguarding patients from unsafe practices. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h1)

question: Professional accountability in nursing best refers to what obligation?

options.A: Answering for your own clinical actions and omissions
options.B: Paying financial penalties for hospital equipment breakdown
options.C: Following verbal orders from senior doctors without question
options.D: Writing the monthly duty roster for all ward staff

explanation: Accountability requires every nurse to take personal responsibility for the outcomes of their professional decisions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h1)

question: The external obligation to answer for breaches of professional laws is known as what?
explanation: Legal accountability involves answering to formal regulatory councils or courts for violations of professional standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h2)

question: A registered nurse delegates a stable patient's vital signs to a junior worker. Who remains accountable for the patient evaluation?

options.A: The patient relative who agreed to the admission
options.B: The hospital chief medical director on duty
options.C: The junior worker who recorded the vital signs
options.D: The registered nurse who performed the delegation

explanation: Delegation transfers the execution of a task, but the overarching accountability for patient assessment stays with the delegating nurse. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h2)

question: Which supervision type primarily focuses on skill acquisition and professional learning?
explanation: Formative supervision is designed to foster learning, professional development, and clinical skill enhancement. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h3)

question: A nurse supervisor helps a staff member cope with the emotional distress of a sudden patient death. What type of supervision is this?
explanation: Restorative supervision aims to support emotional well-being and help staff recover from workplace stress and trauma. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h3)

question: What does the 'Right Person' principle in clinical delegation refer to?

options.A: Ensuring the staff member has the correct training and skill level
options.B: Selecting a patient relative who is willing to assist with feeding
options.C: Assigning the ward manager to handle all emergency admissions
options.D: Choosing the nurse with the longest years of experience in the hospital

explanation: The right person principle ensures that tasks are only given to staff competent to execute them safely. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h4)

question: A nurse asks an unqualified cleaner to administer oral medication to a patient. Which right of delegation is violated?
explanation: Administered medication requires specific clinical training, making a cleaner the wrong person for this task. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h4)

question: Which body is legally responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body empowered by law to regulate all cadres of nursing and midwifery in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h5)

question: Why is it vital for a nurse supervisor to know the legal scope of practice?

options.A: To ensure doctors complete their ward rounds on time every morning
options.B: To determine the procurement schedule for hospital medical supplies
options.C: To prevent subordinates from performing tasks outside their legal training
options.D: To calculate correct monthly salaries for all hospital nursing staff

explanation: Understanding the scope of practice prevents illegal task performance and protects patients from unqualified interventions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is a major organizational barrier to effective clinical supervision in busy hospitals?

options.A: Severe staff shortages and high patient-to-nurse ratios
options.B: Excessive availability of advanced leadership training programs
options.C: Too many hours allocated specifically for mentorship sessions
options.D: Complete absence of any administrative paperwork on wards

explanation: Heavy workloads and staff shortages leave senior nurses with little time to supervise and mentor junior colleagues. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h6)

question: How does a toxic hierarchical work culture negatively affect clinical accountability?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any formal nursing council oversight
options.B: It makes junior staff afraid to report mistakes or ask for guidance
options.C: It forces doctors to perform routine nursing documentation duties
options.D: It ensures that every ward error is instantly published in journals

explanation: Fear of harsh punishment in a rigid hierarchy causes staff to hide errors rather than seek help or learn from them. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of a blame-free incident reporting culture in healthcare?

options.A: Learning from system errors to prevent future patient harm
options.B: Ensuring that no staff member ever faces disciplinary review
options.C: Hiding clinical mistakes from hospital management and patients
options.D: Transferring all legal liability away from the employing hospital

explanation: A safety culture prioritizes systemic analysis and learning over punitive measures when errors occur. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h7)

question: Why is root-cause analysis preferred over quick punishment after a clinical error?

options.A: It uncovers underlying system flaws that allowed the error to happen
options.B: It ensures that nursing supervisors never have to write incident reports
options.C: It guarantees that patients receive financial compensation immediately
options.D: It speeds up the process of discharging stable patients from the ward

explanation: Root-cause analysis looks beyond the individual nurse to fix broken processes and prevent repeated mistakes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h7)
